reason: This text from Exodus 14 depicts the Israelites actively and openly expressing their views throughout. In verse 14:10-12, they explicitly voice their complaints to Moses: 'And they said to Moses, Was it not enough that you took us to die in the wilderness? What have you done to us to bring us out of Egypt?' They freely articulate their fears ('and they were very afraid and cried out to the Lord'), their concerns about their impending deaths, and their preference to return to Egyptian slavery. The narrative provides direct quotation of their speech, showing no discouragement or suppression of their voices. Additionally, they appeal directly to God through prayer and lamentation. The text exemplifies a people who are freely and openly expressing their anxieties, doubts, and perspectives despite their perilous circumstances.
